label: PTC read-through agents, amlexanox and class
LDH inhibition or lowering (stiripentol, LDHA tool compounds, oligonucleotide)
ACTH, corticosteroids and phenobarbital-containing regimens (class level)
d-APV (a tool compound; the only agent with a WWOX readout) and the NMDAR/AMPAR class (memantine, perampanel, radiprodil and others are untested siblings)

The HIF axis in the glycolytic shift: genetic HIF1A and EPAS1 knockdown and a PX-478-class lever, with a prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitor as a conditional arm (direction conditional, not established as the disease direction; a mechanism experiment, not a treatment)
Belnacasan (caspase-1 inhibitor prodrug; active acid VRT-043198): gated proposal for the IL-1 axis
Apabetalone (BET inhibitor): conditional proposal for the microglial cytokine axis
Sulfopin (covalent PIN1 probe): mechanism experiment on MYC, after a MYC-specific lever
Roxadustat (HIF prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitor): dropped as a lever on label and pharmacology grounds (seizures, thyromimetic action, rat brain necrosis, no paediatric data), not on direction
AR-12 (reference: PDPK1, not a PDH-kinase hit)

The NRF2 (KEAP1) axis in WWOX-deficient neural cells: a genetic KEAP1/NFE2L2 arm, omaveloxolone and monomethyl/dimethyl fumarate as two chemotypes (a role-resolving mechanism experiment, not a treatment)
Voclosporin (calcineurin inhibitor): dropped; label names seizure and PRES, and its TNF seed is the non-significant one
PF-03758309 (pan-PAK inhibitor; reference: dominated by the direct NRF2 arm)
CDDO-EA (NRF2-activator analogue; class precedent in adult rat seizure models, not transferable to omaveloxolone)
